title: An invariant affine open around generic orbit points cut out by an element of I, for finite finitely presented groupoids with an immersion into an affine scheme

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-find-almost-invariant-function (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 2922-2933

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Choose V' around the generic orbit points as in the invariant-affine-open lemma; since U without V is closed, j is an immersion and V(I) union j(U) is closed, there is an ideal J inside I with V(J) = V(I) union j(U without V), for instance the ideal of elements of I vanishing on j(U without V); replacing the groupoid, j and I by their restrictions to V' with J, one may assume U is affine and s, t finite locally free. Pick f in I not vanishing at any point of the R-orbits of u_1, ..., u_m (algebra silly lemma) and form the norm g = Norm_s of t^sharp composed with j^sharp(f). Since f in I and V(I) union j(U) is closed, U intersect D(f) to D(f) is a closed immersion, hence f^n g is the image of an element h in I for some n > 0. By the determinant trick lemma g is R-invariant, so D(g) is R-invariant; f does not vanish on the orbit of u_j, so g does not vanish at u_j; and V(g) contains V(j^sharp(f)), whence j^{-1}D(h) = D(g), an R-invariant affine open containing the orbit points. (source lines 2935-2962)

core_obligations: Reduction: take u_1, ..., u_m in V' inside V inside U as in lemma-invariant-affine-open-around-generic-point; U without V is closed, j is an immersion and V(I) union j(U) is closed, so an ideal J inside I with V(J) = V(I) union j(U without V) exists, e.g. the ideal of elements of I vanishing on j(U without V); replace (U, R, s, t, c), j and I by (V', R', s', t', c'), j|_{V'} and J, so that U is affine and s, t are finite locally free (proof lines 2936-2946). Construction: pick f in I not vanishing at any point of the R-orbits of u_1, ..., u_m by algebra-lemma-silly; set g = Norm_s(t^sharp(j^sharp(f))) in Gamma(U, O_U); since f in I and V(I) union j(U) is closed, U intersect D(f) to D(f) is a closed immersion, hence f^n g is the image of an element h in I for some n > 0 (proof lines 2947-2955). Verification: groupoids-lemma-determinant-trick makes g R-invariant and D(g) R-invariant; g does not vanish at u_j because f does not vanish on its orbit; V(g) contains V(j^sharp(f)), so j^{-1}D(h) = D(g), giving the R-invariant affine open containing u_1, ..., u_m (proof lines 2956-2961).
proof_roadmap: Restrict to the invariant affine neighbourhood V' of the orbit generic points and adjust the ideal to J inside I (proof lines 2936-2946).
Choose f in I avoiding the finitely many orbit points and form the norm g of the pullback of f (proof lines 2947-2952).
Produce h in I with j^{-1}D(h) = D(g) using the closed immersion U intersect D(f) into D(f) and the norm relation f^n g (proof lines 2953-2955).
Verify invariance via the determinant trick and nonvanishing at the orbit points (proof lines 2956-2961).
